chapter: Hopkins, the South and Stuff Smith
title: Dating his joining Fats, and taking Claude Hopkins dates while Fats was idle
summary: He started moving with Fats in 1934; when Fats was in town with nothing happening, he got Fats's permission to play West Virginia dates with Claude Hopkins.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: In the late thirties -- when did you join Fats, in '34?
When I did?
Yeah.
Who, me?
Yeah, you. '34?
Uh, yeah, we started -- let me see --
I think that's when he started --

'33, it was '33 or '34, the latter part of the two. It was so close together there, and I do know we started moving together in '34. Right? It was 30 -- maybe the latter -- a few days in '33, maybe, because I was in New York, I had just come to New York. I had quit Doc Hyder's band, you know, and I was -- had come into New York, you know?
But then there was -- then there was that period when you were with Fletcher Henderson.
Yes. Yeah.
Yeah, now when were you with Claudet Hopkins? How did that come about?
Fats went to Europe, and one of those times he went to Europe, two or three times --
First time, or what?
Uh, no, couldn't have been the first time, because --
What did you do the first time when he went?

Same thing, hang around and, you know, work wherever I could. Grab club dates, or whatnot, you know, and there wasn't a hell of a lot then, for me, as a colored guy, I'll put it that way. They -- well, there weren't too many colored club dates, anyway.

So Claud needed somebody. Claud was going to -- where? -- West Virginia. He had some dates in West Virginia, here and there. And he asked me to make them with him. So I asked Fats. Fats gone, so I said Fats, is it all right for me to make these dates? He say yeah, go ahead.
Had Fats gone to Europe, or is it -- was he still in the States?
Yeah, he had gone and come back.
Oh come back, I see.
Yeah, he was here then.
So you were working with Fats again.

Yeah, but I mean we're in town and nothing happening, we were sitting around and I don't know for what reason. I don't know if he didn't feel like going out, or what, because he could always -- well I want to go here, go there, and point, and that's where they sent us. You know?
And he said go ahead, I'll let you know. I said just let me know when you're ready, and wherever I am, I'll come in. He said oh, don't worry about it.
